title: Choose the home page structure
question: Same black, crimson and brass shop; three ways to build the front page. The roll dealt The Letterboard. Keep it, take another, steer, or re-roll.

options.label: The Letterboard
options.lineage: the black felt letterboard on a barbershop wall
options.thesis: The shop's felt letterboard, spelled live from the database, is the first thing anyone reads.
options.viewport: The crimson wall runs edge to edge; the logo sign hangs top-left over a wall-sized letterboard that spells today's hours, paid sales, barbers in and prices, with Open the POS on its rail.
options.risk: Gimmicky if every heading turns into letters; the letters stay on two boards only (today and the directory).

raised.raise: The crimson wall owns the first viewport and leaves the frame on both sides instead of sitting in a rounded card.
Today's figures read as identical units shoulder to shoulder, one sweep of the eye.
Sign, board and wall sit on separate depth planes that drift apart slightly as you scroll (frozen under reduced motion).

options.label: The Pole and Its Signs
options.lineage: projecting blade signs on a shop street
options.thesis: One barber pole runs the height of the page and turns as you scroll; every section hangs off it as a blade sign.
options.viewport: A full-height pole stands at the left; the logo sign hangs off its first bracket, the hook and Open the POS beside it, and Today hangs from the next bracket at the fold.
options.risk: Bends the rule that the pole is a state light into 'the pole shows how far you've scrolled'; on phones it shrinks to a thin rail at the edge.

options.label: The Station
options.lineage: a barber's station seen from the chair
options.thesis: The page is the station: the LED mirror holds the shop's sign, the counter holds the tools, and the owner's tools sit in a locked drawer.
options.viewport: A chrome-bezel LED mirror fills the top and reflects the crimson wall and the sign; on the counter below, Open the POS, Shift Log and End-of-Day Cash lie as tool plates beside a brass-locked owner drawer.
options.risk: Tools-as-objects can tip into costume; the counter has to stay a row of plainly labelled links.

options.label: Zoo Guide Map
options.lineage: a zoo and gardens guide map
options.thesis: The shop as a map of swelling colour lobes.
options.viewport: One lobe per screen, coastline dividing sections.
options.case: Fuses poorly: barbers and the panel don't read the shop as a map.
options.kept: One region owns the first screen and leaves the frame on two sides.

options.label: VU Meter Bridge
options.thesis: Today's numbers as a row of meters.
options.viewport: A row of needles for the day's figures.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a shop isn't a studio, and needles blur exact counts.
options.kept: Identical units shoulder to shoulder, read in one sweep.

options.label: Multiplane Cel Dawn
options.thesis: The page as painted planes at different depths.
options.case: Fuses partly: depth fits the shop interior, but painted scenery is a picture, not the shop.
options.kept: Separate depth planes drifting at different rates on scroll.

options.label: Moiré Gallery
options.case: Fuses poorly: loses the crimson and brass the owner chose.
options.kept: One caption per canvas; nothing competes with the object.

options.label: Suminagashi Basin
options.thesis: The page as a fluid surface.
options.case: Fuses poorly: no tie to the shop, and WebGL on LAN phones.
options.kept: The newest item carries the most contrast.

options.label: Glaze River Shelf
options.viewport: A row of cups with recipe cards.
options.case: Fuses poorly: nothing in the shop's day maps to glaze runs.
